text:
Hi,
Marine mammals handle hydration a bit differently from land mammals. Whales, dolphins and porpoises swallow seawater, and their kidneys are far more efficient than ours at keeping water while getting rid of salt. In many species, the salt load leaves as concentrated urine, so drinking ocean water is not a bad move for them. Seals and sea lions have salt glands, usually above the eye; these secrete brine through small pores, and the fluid can run onto the fur. Some pinnipeds drink at the surface, others get enough from food and metabolic water.
The size point matters. A larger mammal loses water more slowly because surface area scales slower than mass, so a whale can stay underwater for long stretches without needing to surface and gulp. I know that sounds odd, but the salt handling is the special part; it is not like a human drinking a glass of seawater. The main thing is that they are not avoiding seawater; they process it in their bodies and use the water. That combination is why some species can live in very salty conditions and get along. You can think of it as a body tuned for salt, not a thirst problem.
Thanks
